name: CR-Int-13-parts-2.b
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
If \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) -
 F(b).\]

So, we need to calculate \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}.\]

Using integration by parts, that is if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of {{CT:4}} then \[\int u dv = uv - \int v du,\] by defining \(u = {{CT:5}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that

\(du = {{CT:7}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:8}}\).

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}\left[{{CT:8}}\right] - \int \left[{{CT:8}}\right]{{CT:7}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}}
 \end{array}\]

So, let \(F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:12}}\)

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}} - {{CT:14}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:15}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number.  This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
